properties.description: A cycle finding names what it walked (crates/reflow2-core/tests/cycles.rs) — 6 new cases of 15. A loop through ONE shared contract names that contract and says no DEPENDS_ON is involved; a genuine TWO-contract service cycle is NOT blamed on the model but still names both; a plain DEPENDS_ON tangle says it is direct and names no contract; a MIXED cycle claims neither pure case, because saying 'no DEPENDS_ON' there would send a reader to check their interface model while real code coupling sits in the loop. PLUS the medium pair, which is the case that matters: a round trip through two library/data contracts reports the medium, and THE SAME SHAPE over REST makes no foundation claim — without that counterweight the medium sentence would print on every contract cycle and mean nothing.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS: collapse the interface-count discriminator and exactly the two-contract counterweight fails; drop interface attribution entirely (the pre-BL-141 behaviour) and exactly the three tests naming the new behaviour fail while the direct-DEPENDS_ON case stays green; force the foundation-medium claim always-true and exactly the REST counterweight fails. THE DESIGN WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT, not reasoning: the first discriminator keyed on the INTERFACE COUNT (one shared contract = coarse model), and reproducing the reporter's own cycle on their real design showed it misses their actual case — their loop runs through TWO interfaces and is structurally identical to a genuine service cycle. Only the `medium` separates them. Verified end to end by reconstructing their pre-workaround model from a read-only snapshot of their live graph: the exact loop they reported, `cmp:fundamental-detection → cmp:midi-renderer → cmp:fundamental-detection`, now names both contracts and the medium.
properties.name: A cycle finding names what it walked
